answers.q1: pip with a venv, driven by the repo's scripts (no uv/poetry). Install with: scripts/install. It creates ./venv and runs pip install -U pip, then pip install -r requirements.txt. The scripts use venv/bin/ automatically if venv exists.
answers.q2: scripts/test. Locally it runs scripts/check first, then coverage run -m pytest, then scripts/coverage, which fails under 100% coverage. In CI the lint step is skipped here because it runs separately. For pytest alone with no lint or coverage gate, run: venv/bin/pytest
answers.q3: venv/bin/pytest tests/client/test_auth.py (or plain 'pytest tests/client/test_auth.py' if the venv is activated). The wrapper also works: scripts/test tests/client/test_auth.py, but it adds lint and the 100% coverage gate.
answers.q4: scripts/check. It runs these in order: ./scripts/sync-version, venv/bin/ruff format httpx tests --diff, venv/bin/mypy httpx tests, venv/bin/ruff check httpx tests. To auto-fix instead, run scripts/lint (ruff check --fix, then ruff format).
answers.q5: No source files are vendored or hand-generated. Build and tool output must not be edited, and all of it is gitignored: venv*/, build/, dist/, site/ (mkdocs output), htmlcov/, .coverage, *.egg-info/, .mypy_cache/, .pytest_cache/, __pycache__/. Related files to leave alone: httpx/__version__.py must match the latest CHANGELOG.md entry, because scripts/sync-version checks this. requirements.txt is also a pinned dependency list.
